Hanley & Roche

Barristers & Solicitors · 1801 Hollis Street, Suite 1400 · Halifax, Nova Scotia · B3J 3N4
19 August 2026

WITHOUT PREJUDICE
DELIVERED BY EMAIL

Ms. Wren Castellanos
[address on file]

RE: Estate of Alden Joseph Furey — Recordings made at Oakmount Manor

Dear Ms. Castellanos,

We are solicitors for Mr. Derek Furey, in his personal capacity and as Executor of the Estate of the late Alden Furey (the “Estate”).

We are instructed that during the production of a documentary film at Oakmount Manor between March and July 2026 you created audio recordings of the late Mr. Furey, who at the material time was a resident living with a diagnosis of dementia and for whom our client acted as substitute decision-maker.

Our client has requested copies of these recordings and their destruction thereafter. We are instructed that this request has been refused. We are further instructed that you have suggested to our client that the recordings contain statements which you consider to be of a serious nature. We put you on notice that any statement attributed to the late Mr. Furey was made, if at all, by a man lacking testamentary and general capacity, is inherently unreliable, and is not to be published, distributed, broadcast, or provided to any third party, including any police service or member of the Mahar family.

We hereby DEMAND that you: (1) deliver to this office all copies of any recording of the late Mr. Furey; (2) permanently destroy any copies within your possession or control; and (3) provide written confirmation of the foregoing, within FOURTEEN (14) DAYS of the date of this letter.

Should you fail to comply, our client reserves all rights, including proceedings for breach of the participant agreement, breach of privacy, and defamation of the late Mr. Furey and of our client.

Govern yourself accordingly.

Yours truly,

HANLEY & ROCHE

Siobhan Roche
Per: S. Roche

notes before the call with Marguerite (Stewart McKelvey, via Colin)

- I am a contractor on the film. participant agreement covers me. good.
- their letter demands I destroy recordings that may be evidence of an indictable offence. everyone agrees you can't be compelled to do that.
- the 'no capacity' argument: for a WILL, sure. for an excited/unprompted utterance about a crime, capacity works differently — it goes to weight, not admissibility. Paul's point. Marguerite to confirm.
- what I actually want from her: a one-line reply that says 'our client will not be destroying anything and considers your client's demand improper given the subject matter', and nothing else. no detail. don't tell them what's on it. they can guess.
- ask: do I have any exposure for having emailed Maureen before HRP formally opened? Paul thinks no. I did it anyway. I'd do it again.
